People say this every year. What I think is happening is that 1) people's Steam library keeps getting bigger every year and will therefore already contain most of the titles they are interested in which are currently on sale and 2) people will probably already own fairly new titles that are currently on sale because they might have pre-ordered them at a discount (as that practice has become increasingly popular in the last couple of years) or bought them at an earlier sale this year (as sales throughout the year have become more common in the last couple of years).

There really is a shitload of games on sale right now, and browsing through them I've found that I already own most of the games I'm interested in (because of the two reasons mentioned above), but pretty much all games I can think of are on a huge discount, so it's not the sale that's the problem, it's that I already own most games I'm interested in.

$7.50 is an excellent price for XCOM, especially given this game's replay-value, but you said yourself that you essentially already own and have played through the game. If you raise the bar of judging a Steam sale to "is it so good that it makes you buy games you already played or own again and again?" then, yes, I guess you could say this year's Steam sale is underwhelming. Whether that's a reasonable standard or not I'll leave for yourself to judge.

This is basically it. I've bought a couple games that I did already own/have already played because I built my own PC, but I pretty much own everything I want to own at this point. It's not just you. No Flash Sales or limited time offers may mean that people can buy the games they want wherever they want without having to fear it will later be available with a larger discount, but it also removes much of the excitement people felt over the event, and I'd argue that it also lowers the discounts publishers are willing to give for individual titles.

Plus, the highlighted deals this year are rather...meh. Most of them are fairly old, there's the odd sticker like Evolve, the Thief remake, or Risen, various niche indie titles such as The Talos Principle, and then someone thinks it a good idea to put up G-Mod, which at this point could almost be thrown at the players for free.

What blockbusters are you missing on sale? Browsing through EA, Ubisoft, etc.'s catalog, I found hardly any game not on sale. Even things like Rainbow Six Siege or Fallout 4, which have been out just a bit over a month (or less than that) are on sale, even if only slightly discounted, but most big publisher's games are on -50%, just from briefly skimming over stuff. I can find all the GTAs, Assassin's Creeds, Witchers and Call of Duties (whose discount amounts have always been a joke, btw) on sale just fine.

I guess you could complain that releases that are just barely over a month old are "only" like 17% discounted, like Fallout 4, but the truth is that holiday releases of the same season were always barely on sale, if at all, and huge sales of very recently released titles were always somewhat an anomaly. I think some Borderlands game or DLC might have been like 50% off only barely a month after its release at some point, but again, that was an anomaly.

The lack of flash sales is a mixed bag. I can see the excitement aspect you mentioned, but on the other hand there were many, many people complaining about that practice in the past because they saw it as a scam if they happened to buy a game at one point which got further discounted just a day later, for a brief period of time. Yes, most "smart" Steam customers knew never to buy anything until the very last day of the sale and wait until a game might pop up as a daily or flash special, but not everyone knows that (especially people new to Steam) and you can make an argument that this is also a stupid practice and it's a legitimate annoyance, especially for people who can't check / access the Steam store every day during the sales period. It seems like Valve is in a damned if you do, damned if you don't situation here, no matter what they do, they'll always get one group of customers complaining.

Honestly, for me, the lack of flash/daily deals kills a lot of the excitement. Spreading it out and me wondering what was next was really engaging. Sure it was a hassle but, the whole "maybe {whatever game I was excited for} is next up" was so much more exciting.
